observation.visible_scene: A round stone basin (birdbath) filled with calm water, viewed at an oblique angle. A vertical stack of about six smooth blue-grey stones stands in the upper-centre of the water, with its mirror reflection directly below it. The water surface reflects a pale sky with clouds, a bare branching tree on the left, and leafy trees on the right; dry reeds/grass ring the basin at the top of the frame.
visible_changes: The stone stack and the basin rim remain in fixed screen positions throughout the excerpt; the stack does not translate, tilt, or topple.
The reflected sky shifts in colour: from a pale pinkish-white early on to a deeper blue with warmer golden-brown tree reflections on the right toward the end.
A bright sun glare blooms in the upper-right portion of the water reflection, first noticeable around frame 21, strongest in frames 23-28, and fading by frame 30.
The mirror reflection of the stone stack becomes progressively softer and more wavy/distorted across the excerpt, consistent with gentle surface ripples developing on otherwise still water.
The dark reflection of the bare tree on the left persists but its contrast and the colour of the sky behind it change with the lighting.
A faint dark reflection (likely of an off-screen object/photographer) appears in the lower-left water and is most visible during the glare interval.
The reeds at the top change colour tone (green to reddish) without moving, indicating a lighting change rather than object motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: No drop, wind, or other disturbance is visible, so the cause of any surface distortion is unknown.
Whether the glare and ripples continue, grow, or settle after the last frame is not shown.
The state of the water and stack before the first frame is not shown.
uncertain_details: It is unclear whether the increasing waviness of the stack's reflection is true ripple distortion or simply the bright glare washing out the reflected edges.
Minor shifts in the framing of the basin rim could be slight camera drift or could be reflection/lighting changes; camera motion is not confidently established.
The exact moment the glare begins and ends is gradual and frame-dependent.
